newsitem.title: USA: Damark CEO backs consensus EPS estimate.
newsitem.headline: Damark CEO backs consensus EPS estimate.

text.p: Damark International Inc Chief Executive Mark Cohn said Wednesday the company is comfortable estimates of a 25 percent increase in earnings per share for full-year 1997 and a 10 percent increase in sales.

When asked about expectations at the annual shareholders' meeting, Cohn said, "The analysts that follow the company have articulated expectations of 10 percent sales growth and about 25 percent EPS growth. We are very comfortable with those expectations today and, if there's need to revise those upward as the year unfolds, we'll do that."
In 1996, the direct marketing and membership services company earned $0.70 per share on revenues of $513.7 million.
Earlier Wednesday, Damark reported first-quarter earnings of $0.05 per share, above a First Call mean estimate of $0.03 per share.
